What I did: Sent raw HMDA CSVs to the models (1,000 rows ≈ 53K tokens, 5–6 min per call).
Outcome: Too slow and costly, so switched to pre-summarized tables (≈1.5K tokens) with JSON output and re-framed the study around emotional and identity framing. Dropped Qwen for not following instructions.

What I did: 3 models (GPT-3.5, Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 2.5) × control vs emotional × N=300, summary-table input.
Outcome: Claude flipped completely: 0% → 100% YES. Gemini went the other way: 22% → 0% YES. ChatGPT barely moved: 1.3% → 0.3% YES.

What I did: 6 cloud models (Haiku/Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro, GPT-3.5, GPT-4o-mini) × 7 prompts × N=10.
Outcome: Qualitative only. GPT-4o-mini reversed under every treatment and Sonnet said YES to the emotional prompts. Gemini Flash said NO to everything; Gemini Pro split 50/50.

What I did: 12 models (6 cloud + 6 local) × control + 6 framings × N=300, summary-table input. Chi-square/Fisher tests vs control. Unparsed answers were repaired into JSON (originals kept in _backup_pre_repair).
Outcome: Change in YES rate vs control, in percentage points: Sonnet +100 on emotional/extreme/suicidal, GPT-4o-mini +66 to +94 on all framings, Haiku about +71 to +75, Gemma-3 +93 on emotional only. GPT-3.5 moved toward NO. Llama and Qwen2.5 were 0% YES everywhere.

What I did: 4 local models (qwen2.5-7b, gemma-3-12b, llama-3.1-8b, llama-3.2-3b), control prompt, N=10. First test of raw-CSV input with 2,000-row samples, to estimate cost and time.
Outcome: Valid JSON: Qwen 10/10, Gemma 10/10, Llama-3.1 5/10, Llama-3.2 0/10. About 73–147 s per call. Chose 2,000 rows per sample and swapped some models. Full study estimated at ≈ $1,620 for cloud and 3–6 days per local model.

What I did: 6 cloud models × 7 prompts × 16 identities (race × ethnicity × sex × age) × N=3, raw-CSV input (2,000 rows). 935 of 936 calls completed, ≈ $72.
Outcome: Control was 0% YES for every model. Black identities got YES 15.1% vs 4.9% for White (p=3.9e-7); ethnicity and age had no effect. Accuracy couldn't be scored (no variance in ground truth), so the design changed to 4 races × 2 sexes.

What I did: 4 local models on vLLM with guided JSON × 4 prompts (control, emotional, identity, emotional_identity). The identity prompts ran on 8 race × sex identities. N=10 per cell, 720 calls.
Outcome: All 720 answers were NO, so no framing effect anywhere. ≈ 74–103K tokens and 115–288 s per call. Afterwards the prompts were reworded (first-person emotional prompts) and the config moved to N=300.

What I did: qwen3.5-9b on vLLM, N=300 with identity sample split (8 race × sex identities, 37–38 samples each), using the reworded prompts (run_qwen.job). 1,200 calls.
Outcome: Almost all NO: 1,196 NO, 2 YES (1 control, 1 emotional), 2 unparsed. YES rate is 0.3% for control and emotional and 0% for every identity cell, so again no framing effect. ≈ 103K tokens and 350–415 s per call.
